unit.title: Systems and Simultaneous Constraints
unit.act: Act V - Satisfying several conditions at once
unit.role: Extend linear reasoning to multiple equations, variables, and feasible regions.
unit.governingQuestion: Which values satisfy several requirements simultaneously?
unit.storyArc: Intersections represent simultaneous truth. Graphing estimates solutions, substitution replaces equals by equals, elimination combines equations to remove a variable, and applications reveal when two variables are the natural model.
outcomes: Interpret a system solution as satisfying every constraint.
Solve systems graphically, by substitution, and by elimination.
Classify one, zero, or infinitely many solutions.
Model totals, mixtures, rates, and break-even situations.
Graph systems of inequalities and interpret feasible regions.
unit.investigation: Design a production or allocation plan subject to budget, time, and minimum-output constraints.
unit.mastery: Mixed systems require method selection and interpretation of the ordered-pair solution.

expositionBeats: Open with: Locate feasible production or scheduling choices.
Let the anchor figure establish the quantities and the question before introducing compressed notation.
Develop the mechanism explicitly and name the property, definition, or reversible operation that justifies each rewrite.
Coordinate verbal, numerical, graphical, and algebraic representations wherever they are meaningful.
Return to the opening and state what the new structure now makes possible, including restrictions and a check.
examples: Foundation example: a clean numerical case that isolates the decision in systems of inequalities.
Representation example: apply the same idea to the opening scene, a graph, table, or diagram and require a complete sentence of interpretation.
Transfer example: combine systems of inequalities with an earlier skill so the learner must select the method rather than imitate a nearby pattern.
misconceptions: Applying a remembered rule without checking whether its structural conditions hold.
Producing a numerical result without interpreting units, domain, or whether the result answers the original question.
previous.bridgeForward: The closing paragraph should make systems strategy studio feel like the next necessary question.

unit.title: Systems and Simultaneous Constraints
unit.act: Act V - Satisfying several conditions at once
unit.role: Extend linear reasoning to multiple equations, variables, and feasible regions.
unit.governingQuestion: Which values satisfy several requirements simultaneously?
unit.storyArc: Intersections represent simultaneous truth. Graphing estimates solutions, substitution replaces equals by equals, elimination combines equations to remove a variable, and applications reveal when two variables are the natural model.
outcomes: Interpret a system solution as satisfying every constraint.
Solve systems graphically, by substitution, and by elimination.
Classify one, zero, or infinitely many solutions.
Model totals, mixtures, rates, and break-even situations.
Graph systems of inequalities and interpret feasible regions.
unit.investigation: Design a production or allocation plan subject to budget, time, and minimum-output constraints.
unit.mastery: Mixed systems require method selection and interpretation of the ordered-pair solution.
